items.title: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Trailer: Sacha Baron Cohen Reprises A Modern Classic Character In New Film From Amazon MGM Studios
items.summary:
Amazon MGM Studios has released the first trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I?, the comedy that brings Sacha Baron Cohen back to the character he built his early career on. The film opens in theaters worldwide on Oct. 23, and until the trailer arrived its plot had been kept quiet.

The project also marks Baron Cohen's first time directing a feature. As Deadline reported, word of the film only surfaced through a leak last month, and Baron Cohen fueled the speculation when he turned up at Wimbledon in character.

Ali G, the British hip-hop poseur, first appeared on Channel 4's The 11 O'Clock Show in 1998 before graduating to Da Ali G Show, which ran one season on Channel 4 and then two more on HBO. The character already headlined one movie, Ali G Indahouse, a Universal Pictures comedy that Baron Cohen co-wrote and starred in.

Who Iz I? puts Baron Cohen back with Amazon MGM after Borat Subsequent Moviefilm, the sequel that landed on Prime Video during the pandemic and picked up two Oscar nominations. This time the studio is going the theatrical route rather than straight to streaming.

The October release date gives Amazon MGM a fall comedy slot and gives Baron Cohen his first credit as a feature director. No further plot details have been made public.

items.title: Tom Hiddleston Thriller ‘Tenzing’ To Open Zurich Film Festival
items.summary:
The Zurich Film Festival will open its 22nd edition on September 24 with Tenzing, a Mount Everest thriller starring Tom Hiddleston and Willem Dafoe. Both actors plan to attend the European premiere alongside director Jennifer Peedom, whose previous documentaries include Sherpa and Mountain.

The Apple Original Films project tells the true story of Tenzing Norgay, the Himalayan mountaineer who reached the 8,849-meter summit of Everest in 1953 with New Zealand alpinist Edmund Hillary. Genden Phuntsok plays Norgay and Hiddleston plays Hillary, with Thinley Lhamo as Norgay's wife Dawa and Caitríona Balfe as expedition secretary Jill Henderson.

The film's conflict turns on status as much as altitude. Norgay and Henderson press Colonel John Hunt, played by Dafoe, to make Norgay a full member of the British expedition rather than support staff, and the climb plays out against differences of class and belief, with Western climbers treating the mountain as a conquest and Norgay revering it as a sacred goddess.

Festival director Christian Jungen tied the selection to this year's programming theme. "This year's ZFF motto is dream big," he said in a statement, adding that the first ascent "only succeeded because the climbers respected the local Sherpa people and the laws of nature."

Deadline reported the opening-night booking, which follows other festival announcements including a Golden Eye Award for Naomi Watts and gala slots for Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky and the Channing Tatum film Josephine. The Zurich Film Festival runs September 24 through October 4, 2026.

items.title: Shudder To Think Announce New EP Who Sent You?: Hear The Title Track
items.summary:
Shudder To Think, the Washington, DC art-punk band that formed in 1986 and split a decade later, will release a three-song EP called Who Sent You? next month. The title track is out now, and Stereogum reported that the record arrives via Dischord Records, the label that issued the band's early work before they signed to Epic for 1994's Pony Express Record.

The EP follows a two-song single the band put out last year, Thirst Walk b/w Playback, which was their first new music in 27 years. Who Sent You? rounds out with "Something To Do" and "Release The Ball."

Frontman Craig Wedren traced the title track back to his adolescence before he moved to DC. "'Who Sent You?' is about my teenage years in Cleveland in the 1980s, just before I moved to DC with my outsized emotions – young, horny, bored," he said, describing it as "a nocturnal THANK YOU to all of the girls, family, friends, music, and invisible hands that lit the path, angels and devils both."

Wedren spent the years after the breakup scoring films and television, and the band has reunited for tours twice, in 2008 and again in 2025. Three September dates are on the books: Philadelphia's First Unitarian Church on the 11th, New York's Bowery Ballroom on the 12th, both with Miss Grit, and the Masonic Lodge at Hollywood Forever Cemetery in Los Angeles on the 20th.

items.title: Queens of the Stone Age Announce New Album Perfecth, Unveil Single “Insignificant Other”: Stream
items.summary:
Queens of the Stone Age have confirmed their ninth album, Perfecth, arriving October 30th through Matador Records. The band paired the announcement with a new single, "Insignificant Other," which follows last month's "Easy Street."

The record follows 2023's In Times New Roman and was produced by frontman Josh Homme with bassist Michael Shuman. Consequence noted that the album was teased last week in a bloody promo video featuring Homme and guitarist-keyboardist Dean Fertita, though that clip listed a September 30th release date that has since proved inaccurate.

Homme described the new single as "a song about distance," adding that it concerns "how someone can be your entire world only to simply vanish. And about the strange vertigo of being on the receiving end of that." On the title, he offered: "Nothing in this world is perfect, but everything seems to be perfecth. And that title is funny when you're in a group, but it ain't so funny when you're alone."

The nine-track album runs from "It's Only Love" through "Run Away From The Mob," with song titles including "Where The Goth Girls At?," "Mono" and "Phantom Limb." Homme said the variety is deliberate: "Every song sounds like it's from a different world," he said, describing an attempt to "stitch together all these emotions revolving around love, lust, foolishness."

Pre-orders are open in several formats, among them a limited deluxe gatefold edition packaged with handwritten lyrics, stationery, stamps in a custom envelope and a piece of art tucked into a pocket. The band also released a comedic promo clip called "Big Chongus" starring the members and their pets.

Queens of the Stone Age begin the second leg of their North American tour opening for Foo Fighters on September 15th in Regina, Saskatchewan.

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo Officially Releases New Song “serena joy” on Streaming
items.summary:
Olivia Rodrigo has put "serena joy" on streaming services, moving a song that had been available only on a limited CD single to every major platform. The track was cut from the tracklist of her album you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love.

Rodrigo first released the song on Friday, August 22nd, pressing 500 CD singles and selling them exclusively through an independent record store in Tustin, California. Consequence reported that the run sold out within hours.

The song draws on Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale and takes aim at complicity in oppressive systems. It opens with the lines "Yeah, it's all for the cause/ For the good of us all/ And if you close your eyes/ Then it can't be your fault," and later delivers the blunter warning, "If they do it to them, they'll do it to you."

Rodrigo will play the song live for the first time on Saturday, August 29th at Daisy Chain Fields, her new festival in Irvine, California. The lineup includes Chappell Roan, The Breeders, KATSEYE, Doechii, Bikini Kill and Mitski, and organizers scheduled the sets without overlaps.

Her third album, you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, came out on June 12th. Her Unraveled Tour, a sold-out world run, begins September 25th.
